brief: Stained wood, Japanese house. Assume there was a murder there; the house has been abandoned for 5 years.
design_notes: Japanese homes sit lower and furniture is lower: body 1.4 studs, stubby 0.2-stud legs. It reads closer to a tansu chest than a mid-century American console.

Stained wood: kaki-shibu (persimmon tannin) stain on zelkova, a deep reddish-brown with dark grain. One wood for the whole piece, as a tansu would have; the fronts are a touch warmer so they still read as separate panels.
Hardware: black forged iron, as on tansu. Five years in a closed, humid house means rust blooms, worst in crevices.

Five years abandoned: a heavy dust layer on every upward-facing surface, grime packed into seams, stain rubbed off the edges and corners (from years of use before), water rings and stains from a leaking roof.

The murder: dried, oxidised blood, near-black brown, not bright red. A smear over the top-left edge running down across the drawer fronts in drips, as if someone fell against it. Kept to one area. It's a story detail, not a coat of paint.
